extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in algebraic topology (readers learning about fibrations, Postnikov towers, and obstruction theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and constructive criteria for fibrations, path-space constructions, Postnikov and Moore–Postnikov towers, k-invariants, and obstruction theory used to build/approximate spaces and to analyze extension/lifting problems in algebraic topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of cohomology by Eilenberg–MacLane spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural isomorphism H^n(X; G) ≈ [X, K(G,n)] holds for CW complexes; under this isomorphism a class in H^n(X;G) is f*(α) for some map f:X→K(G,n) and a fundamental class α∈H^n(K(G,n);G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take α = T(11) (T the natural isomorphism applied to the identity on K(G,n)); then for any f, T([f]) = f*(α). This allows reducing many cohomological questions to the universal example K(G,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental class as cellular cocycle
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CW model K of K(G,n) with (n−1)-skeleton a point, the fundamental class α∈H^n(K;G) is represented by the cellular cocycle that assigns to each n-cell the element of π_n(K)=G determined by the characteristic map of that cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the identification hn(K) ≈ Ker d (cellular coboundary), the identity element corresponds to inclusion of the n-skeleton; the cocycle evaluation on n-cells gives the coefficient in G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce global cohomology properties to universal example
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove a cohomological property for every space X, show it for the universal class α in H^n(K(G,n);G) and use naturality: every class in H^n(X;G) is f*(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: α↦α^2 map H^1(–;Z)→H^2(–;Z) is zero for all X because for K(Z,1)=S^1 the square α^2 vanishes (H^2(S^1)=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of cup/cross product via Eilenberg–MacLane smash maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Km=K(R,m) and Kn=K(R,n) (R a ring), define cross product/cohomology multiplications by composing X×Y→Km×Kn→Km∧Kn→Km+n with a map µ:Km∧Kn→Km+n inducing R⊗R→R on π_{m+n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define µ using Hurewicz/Künneth isomorphisms on π_{m+n} or as the cohomology class corresponding to the multiplication R⊗R→R. For R=Z one can realize µ by extending the inclusion Sm∧S^n ↪ Km+n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fibration (homotopy lifting property)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map p:E→B is a fibration if it has the homotopy lifting property with respect to all spaces (i.e., any homotopy in B and a lift of its initial time can be lifted to E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fibrations generalize fiber bundles (fibers need not be homeomorphic). Many homotopy-theoretic properties follow from this lifting property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibers over a path component are homotopy equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fibration p:E→B, fibers F_b = p^{-1}(b) over points in the same path component of B are all homotopy equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a path γ in B, lifting a suitable homotopy produces a map L_γ:F_{γ(0)}→F_{γ(1)}; L_γ depends only on homotopy class of γ rel boundary and composes correctly (L_{γγ'} ≃ L_{γ'}∘L_γ), giving homotopy equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of L_γ (path-induced fiber maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If γ≃γ' rel ∂I then L_γ≃L_{γ'}. (b) For path composition L_{γγ'} ≃ L_{γ'}∘L_γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties ensure that L_γ provides well-defined homotopy equivalences of fibers depending only on path-homotopy classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber-preserving map and fiber homotopy equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f:E1→E2 between fibrations p1:E1→B and p2:E2→B is fiber-preserving if p1 = p2∘f. Such an f is a fiber homotopy equivalence if there is a fiber-preserving g:E2→E1 with f∘g and g∘f homotopic to identities through fiber-preserving homotopies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fiber-preserving map that is an ordinary homotopy equivalence is (exercise) a fiber homotopy equivalence; fiber homotopy equivalence may be viewed as a family of homotopy equivalences between corresponding fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback (induced) fibrations and homotopic pullbacks are equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given p:E→B and f:A→B, the pullback f*(E)→A is a fibration; if f_0 and f_1 are homotopic, then f_0^*(E) and f_1^*(E) are fiber homotopy equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by considering the homotopy F:A×I→B and using lifting to show restricted fibrations over A×{0} and A×{1} are fiber homotopy equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local fiber-homotopic triviality over locally contractible base
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is locally contractible then any fibration p:E→B is locally fiber-homotopy equivalent to a product fibration U×F→U over sufficiently small neighborhoods U⊂B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pullback by constant maps and the fact pullbacks along homotopic maps are fiber homotopy equivalent; corollary: fibrations over a contractible base are fiber homotopy equivalent to product fibrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path-space construction factors any map as homotopy equivalence then fibration
rubrics_metrics.description: For f:A→B define Ef = {(a,γ) | γ:I→B, γ(0)=f(a)} with p(a,γ)=γ(1); p:Ef→B is a fibration and the inclusion A↪Ef (constant paths) is a deformation retract, so f factors as A ≃ Ef → B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ef is topologized as subspace of A×B^I. The homotopy fiber F_f of f is the fiber of Ef→B over the basepoint; when f is inclusion Ef is space of paths in B starting in A.

rubrics_metrics.name: If p is a fibration, inclusion E↪Ep is fiber homotopy equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fibration p:E→B the canonical inclusion E↪Ep (path-space construction applied to p) is a fiber homotopy equivalence, so homotopy fibers equal actual fibers up to homotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lifting to build a fiber-preserving homotopy of Ep that retracts into E, showing inclusion is a fiber homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractible total space implies fiber ≃ loopspace of base
rubrics_metrics.description: If F→E→B is a fibration (or fiber bundle) with E contractible, then F→ΩB is a weak homotopy equivalence (i.e., the fiber is weakly equivalent to the loopspace of B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct map F→P B (paths from basepoint) using contraction of E; compare long exact sequences of homotopy groups and apply five-lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Postnikov tower (stages X_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Postnikov tower for path-connected X is ···→X_n→X_{n-1}→··· with (1) X→X_n induces isomorphism on π_i for i≤n, and (2) π_i(X_n)=0 for i>n. One can further require (3) X_n→X_{n-1} be a fibration with fiber K(π_n X,n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every connected CW complex has a Postnikov tower, unique up to homotopy. The X_n can be viewed as (twisted) products of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces; building them uses successive fibrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: k-invariants and building spaces from Postnikov data
rubrics_metrics.description: If X_n→X_{n-1} is the fibration with fiber K(π_n X,n), then X_n is, up to homotopy, the homotopy fiber of a map k_n:X_{n-1}→K(π_{n+1}X,n+2); the cohomology class k_n∈H^{n+2}(X_{n-1};π_{n+1}X) is the nth k-invariant and encodes the twisting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all k_n vanish then X is (weakly equivalent to) the product ∏ K(π_n X,n). In general the k-invariants specify how to assemble X inductively from Eilenberg–MacLane spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for principal Postnikov fibrations
rubrics_metrics.description: A connected CW complex X has a Postnikov tower of principal fibrations iff π1(X) acts trivially on π_n(X) for all n>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal fibration: fibration equivalent (up to weak homotopy) to one appearing as homotopy fiber of a map to K(π,n+1); triviality of π1-action is necessary and sufficient (proved via Lemma 4.70 and identification of relative groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma for realizing CW pair as fibration pair
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (X,A) be a connected CW pair whose homotopy fiber of inclusion A↪X is K(π,n). There exists a fibration F→E→B and a map (X,A)→(E,F) inducing weak homotopy equivalences X→E and A→F iff the action of π1(A) on π_{n+1}(X,A) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If action is trivial use Hurewicz and attach cells to form K(π,n+1) and convert maps to fibrations; five-lemma compares long exact sequences to establish weak equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moore–Postnikov tower for a map f:X→Y
rubrics_metrics.description: A Moore–Postnikov tower is a diagram X→···→Z_n→Z_{n-1}→···→Y with (1) X→Z_n induces isomorphism on π_i for i<n and surjection for i=n; (2) Z_n→Y induces isomorphism on π_i for i>n and injection for i=n; (3) Z_{n+1}→Z_n is a fibration with fiber K(π_n F,n) where F is the homotopy fiber of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every map between connected CW complexes has a Moore–Postnikov tower, unique up to homotopy. One can convert maps to fibrations and use lifting to strictify commutativity. Principal towers exist iff π1(X) acts trivially on π_n(M_f,X) for n>1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstruction theory setup (extension and lifting problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three central problems: Extension Problem (extend A→X to W→X for CW pair (W,A)), Lifting Problem (given fibration X→Y and W→Y find W→X), Relative Lifting Problem (same with extension prescribed on A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obstruction theory produces a sequence of cohomology classes (obstructions) whose vanishing is necessary and (in favorable cases) sufficient for existence of extensions or lifts. Two approaches: cellular step-by-step (cochain-level) or via (Moore-)Postnikov towers (conceptual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse limits of fibrations and homotopy groups (lim and lim^1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sequence of fibrations ···→X_2→X_1 the natural map λ:π_i(lim← X_n)→lim← π_i(X_n) is surjective; λ is injective if π_{i+1}(X_n)→π_{i+1}(X_{n-1}) are surjective for sufficiently large n. There is a natural exact sequence 0→lim^1 π_{i+1}(X_n)→π_i(lim← X_n)→lim← π_i(X_n)→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homotopy lifting to produce compatible representatives for surjectivity; injectivity follows by inductively correcting nullhomotopies when higher π groups stabilize surjectively. This is used to show X→lim← X_n is weak equivalence for Postnikov tower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutativity sign for cup product with Z coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: For R=Z, the commutativity of cup product comes from the degree of the switch map Sm∧S^n→S^n∧Sm, which is (−1)^{mn} acting on Sm+n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sign underlies graded-commutativity of cohomology with integral coefficients and follows from the smash/degree viewpoint of cup product.
